claims.text: A moderate increase in atomic size mismatch enhances dislocation-mediated strengthening in lightweight high-entropy alloys.
A moderate increase in atomic size mismatch promotes formation of a dense, protective oxide scale.
Controlled lattice distortion enables lightweight HEAs to combine low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation stability.
Excessive lattice distortion triggers phase instability and elemental segregation.
The baseline is a primarily single-phase, disordered lightweight HEA with minimal lattice distortion.
Substitution of a principal element by an element with a larger atomic radius will incrementally increase atomic size mismatch.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion modulates dislocation interactions.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion influences nucleation and growth of a passivating oxide layer.
Controlled lattice distortion enhances dislocation pinning and thereby increases yield strength.
Lattice distortion changes oxide-scale formation kinetics so that a more uniform and adherent protective layer forms.
An optimum range of lattice distortion produces simultaneous mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation benefits.
Distortion above the optimum range undermines mechanical properties through phase instability or segregation.
Distortion above the optimum range undermines corrosion and oxidation protection through phase instability or segregation.
A moderately distorted variant will have higher mechanical strength than the minimally distorted baseline.
A moderately distorted variant will have better corrosion resistance than the minimally distorted baseline.
A moderately distorted variant will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than the minimally distorted baseline.
An excessively distorted variant will develop secondary phases.
An excessively distorted variant will exhibit degraded corrosion and oxidation performance.
The hypothesized synergy only operates while a single-phase solid solution is preserved.
Very low lattice mismatch is insufficient to provide the proposed dislocation-strengthening and oxide-scale benefits.
